facts.text: On this date in 1911, the Mona Lisa was reported stolen from the Louvre — and the museum stayed closed for a full week while Paris assumed it had simply been moved for cleaning.
Manila is the world's most densely populated city proper, packing over 110,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any neighborhood in New York or Tokyo.
On this date in 1959, Hawaii became the 50th U.S. state, making it the only state that is entirely an archipelago and the only one located in the tropics.
More people live inside a circle drawn 4,000 km around Bangladesh than outside it — over half of humanity fits within that single radius.

Indonesia spans a wider longitude than the continental United States, yet its capital Jakarta sat on the same sinking coastline that forced the government to begin relocating to a brand-new inland city, Nusantara, in 2024.
On this day in 1986, oil closed below $10 a barrel for the first time in decades — a Saudi-engineered price collapse that wiped out the US shale industry of its era and bankrupted half of Texas.

On August 21, 1888, William Burroughs patented the first commercially viable adding machine, inadvertently laying the hardware foundation for what would become one of America's great computing dynasties.

The NYSE's smallest ever recorded stock price was $0.000625 — a tiny fraction of a cent — yet the exchange still charged its standard minimum trading fee, making the commission worth more than the stock.
Japan's Nikkei 225 peaked in December 1989 at 38,915. It took 35 years to reclaim that level — the longest major index recovery in financial history.

Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway holds more US Treasury bills than the Federal Reserve itself, making a private corporation effectively a larger short-term creditor to the US government than its own central bank.
On this day in 1560, a solar eclipse triggered a panic across Europe precise enough that astronomers later used it to calibrate the drift of Earth's rotation over centuries.
On this day in 1911, the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre — but the theft went unnoticed for 28 hours, because visitors assumed the empty space meant it was being photographed.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Your body contains roughly 37 trillion cells, yet the electrical signal commanding your hand to move travels from brain to fingertip in under 20 milliseconds.
When light enters a black hole, time as measured by an outside observer appears to freeze at the event horizon — the infalling photon seems suspended there forever.
On this day in 1959, Hawaii became the 50th U.S. state — younger than many living Americans, and newer than the Dodgers playing in Los Angeles.
On this day in 1863, Quantrill's Raiders massacred 150 civilians in Lawrence, Kansas — an atrocity larger than the O.K. Corral myth that came to define the Wild West.
The fax machine was invented in 1843, 33 years before the telephone. Alexander Bain patented it while Dickens was writing his fifth novel.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. It was ancient history before Tenochtitlán broke ground.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was as remote from Khufu as we are from Julius Caesar.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012 — too useful to stay invented.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a longing for a home you cannot return to, or one that never was. Untranslatable in a single English word, it carries grief, nostalgia, and belonging all at once.
On this day in 1878, the American Bar Association was founded in Saratoga, New York — giving the legal profession its first formal body and the word 'bar' its institutional permanence.
Petrichor (n.): the scent of rain on dry earth. Named in 1964 by Australian scientists Bear and Thomas, from Greek petra (stone) and ichor, the fluid said to flow in the veins of gods.
On this day in 1911, the Mona Lisa was reported stolen from the Louvre — the word 'heist' gained a masterclass, and the painting became more famous missing than it had ever been hung.
On this date in 2017, Bitcoin's SegWit upgrade activated at block 481,824 — ending a two-year civil war over block size and quietly enabling the Lightning Network's future existence.

On this date in 2012, Ripple Labs was incorporated, pre-dating its own XRP ledger by months and establishing a corporate structure that would later make it the target of the SEC's landmark 2020 securities lawsuit.
Ethereum's gas limit is not set by code — it's a rolling miner (now validator) vote, adjusted block by block. The 'limit' you see is a living negotiation, not a hard cap.
The FBI holds — and periodically auctions — seized Bitcoin. Its 2013 Silk Road seizure of 144,000 BTC made the US government one of the largest single holders on earth at the time.

Bitcoin's timelock script primitive, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, was dormant in the codebase for years before BIP 65 activated it in 2015 — meaning the feature existed on-chain before anyone could legally spend its outputs.

On this date in 2012, the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge results that would crown AlexNet were finalized — its 15.3% top-5 error rate was 10.8 points lower than the runner-up, a margin that effectively ended hand-crafted computer vision.

On this date in 2019, OpenAI released GPT-2's full 1.5B parameter model after a staged rollout it had delayed citing misuse risk — the predicted catastrophe never materialized, quietly retiring the 'staged release' safety argument.

Training GPT-4 is estimated to have cost over $100 million in compute alone. The entire 1969 Apollo program, inflation-adjusted, cost roughly $25 billion — meaning a single model run now consumes what Apollo cost per day.

Transformers were not invented for language. The 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' paper targeted machine translation, and the authors expected the architecture to be a narrow improvement on seq2seq — not the substrate for nearly all frontier AI.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) traces directly to a 1992 paper by Christiano et al.'s predecessor work, but the core mechanism used to align GPT-3 into InstructGPT required fewer than 40,000 human preference labels to shift model behavior measurably.
